name: Population by single year of age
source: Eurostat demo_pjan (1 Jan 2024, 2025) and proj_23np baseline (2027–2045), retrieved 22 Oct 2026; data/manual/FRA_population_by_age.csv
note: 2026 is the 2025 population aged one year (no 2026 vintage yet). Cohort size = people at age 60 in the year the cohort turns 60; mortality between 60 and 64 ignored (≈1% a year).

name: Age of entitlement (AOD) by cohort, law as it stands
Age of entitlement by cohort, 2023 law before suspension
note: Used only to cost the suspension (calibration M5) and to read published repeal costings (M6).

name: Early-career (carrière longue, started before 20) age = AOD − 2, floor 60
source: Law of 14 April 2023: departure two years before the AOD for a start before 20 (four before 18, six before 16)
note: The before-16 and before-18 tiers (58, 60) are folded into the before-20 tier; the durée condition (all quarters) is not modelled.

name: Required insurance duration (durée) 172 quarters from the 1966 cohort
source: COR Table 1.4
note: Not modelled as a separate lever. The RN's 42 annuités (168) would also lower the age for people bound by the durée rather than the floor: omitted, direction = more cost (see U10).

name: Policy start date
source: committee: scenario policy starts in 2028 (D-S18-001 rule 3); a LFSS would take effect 1 September
note: Applies to pensions liquidated from that date; no retroactivity for people already past the new age (they retire at once).

name: '62 for all': AOD 62 for every cohort whose AOD under the law exceeds 62
source: Le Pen, 14–17 Oct 2026 (franceinfo, Europe 1/CNEWS)

name: '60 for early starters': 60 with 40 annuités for a start before 20; 62 for the others
source: Le Pen, 17 Oct 2026; Chenu, RTL 18 Oct 2026; full plan promised 17 Nov 2026
note: The 40-annuité test is assumed met at 60 by everyone who started before 20 (they have 40+ years by 60 by construction, bar career gaps: see B2).

name: '64 resumed': the 2023 path without the suspension
source: Attal/Retailleau positions, Capital 24 Sep 2026
note: Shown as the negative exposure (a saving) for symmetry; the Cour's asymmetry (M4) applies.

name: Share of a cohort bound by the age floor (others)
source: INSEE/FIPECO: at 62 in 2021 (AOD 62) 51% retired, 33% employed, 14% inactive, 3% unemployed; ≈11% had left before 62 (carrière longue)
note: People who liquidate at the AOD itself ≈ 40% of a cohort; the 42-annuité durée adds some. These are the people who move when the floor moves.

name: Share bound among early starters
source: long careers have the durée by 60; DREES: 15% of men and 7% of women liquidate in the year of their 60th birthday

name: Share of a cohort that started work before 20
source: no DREES/CNAV series found for the 1965–75 cohorts; Terra Nova (13 Oct 2026) 'concerne encore tellement de monde sur les dernières cohortes des années 1960'; Montaigne 2024 low case (early starters only) €31.5bn of €34.7bn
note: The single most consequential missing number. Needs the DREES EIC age at first validated quarter by cohort.

name: Of which already eligible to carrière longue under current rules
source: CNAV rapport statistique 2024: 114k RACL departures of 658k new retirees (17%); 1 man in 4, 1 woman in 10
note: These leave at AOD − 2 already; '62 for all' does not move them, '60' moves them by AOD − 2 − 60 (0.75 → 2 years as the AOD rises).

name: Status of the bound before they retire: employed / unemployed / inactive-sick-invalid
source: FIPECO on INSEE 2021: among the non-retired at 62, 66% employed, 6% unemployed, 28% inactive
note: The bound are likelier to be in work than the average non-retired (those who wait for the full rate are employed); the high case reflects that.

name: Gross pension at liquidation
source: DREES, Les retraités et les retraites 2025: new retirees 2023, residents, €1,557 gross droit direct; +2.4% to 2024
note: All compulsory schemes incl. Agirc-Arrco (in S.13). Survivors' pensions excluded.

name: Early starters' pension relative to the average
source: none
note: Long careers at lower wages: full rate but lower SAM. Direction unknown within ±10%.

name: Gross wage of the bound who are employed
source: INSEE 2024: €3,602 gross a month per full-time equivalent, private sector; × 0.85 for part-time at 60–63 (declared)

name: Actual social contributions (D.611 + D.613) as a share of gross wage
source: employer ≈ 39% after the réduction générale at 1.5 SMIC, employee 11.3% (CSG/CRDS excluded: a tax)

name: Taxes on income (CSG/CRDS + IR) on wages / pensions / unemployment benefit
source: CSG/CRDS 9.7% on 98.25% of the wage + IR ≈ 6%; pensions CSG at the average effective 7% (reduced rates) + CRDS/CASA 0.8% + IR ≈ 3%; ARE 6.2% + IR

name: Unemployment benefit (ARE) of the bound who are unemployed
source: Unédic average ARE ≈ €1,300–1,350 gross a month

name: Other benefits (invalidity, sickness, AT-MP, minima) per cohort-person-year
source: DREES for the COR, 27 Jan 2022: a two-year rise in the AOD = +€3.6bn (0.14% GDP) in 2019 on ≈1.6M cohort-person-years; invalidity 1.8bn, minima 0.83bn
note: Applied to the whole cohort's exposure (it embeds the share concerned). Unemployment insurance and prime d'activité are not in it (GF10_5 is costed separately).

name: Indexation of unit costs
source: engine deflator (D-S18-001 rule 4)
note: Pensions index on prices, wages on prices + productivity: a wage-pension gap of ~0.7% a year is ignored to 2040.

name: Lower pension for life from an earlier liquidation
source: COR 2025: the 2023 reform −0.2 pt GDP in 2030 but +0.2 pt in 2070
note: Omitted to 2040; direction = less cost over time, reversing after ~2050.

name: Durée 43 → 42 annuités
source: RN programme
note: Omitted. Would lower the effective age for people bound by the durée (not the floor). Direction = more cost; high case adds 10% to GF10_2.

name: DG Trésor long-run effect of a two-year AOD rise, % GDP
source: DG Trésor note to the COR, 27 Jan 2022, as tabulated by FIPECO (19 Oct 2022): pensions −0.4, pension contributions +0.1, other benefits +0.2, other compulsory levies +0.6, total +0.9 (≈€22bn 2022)
note: Read per cohort-year as half of each (2 cohort-years at steady state). Signs as a saving; the engine flips them for a cut.

name: Time path of the public-balance effect (Mésange) and the OFCE alternative
source: same notes: Mésange 5/10/15/20 years; OFCE e-mod.fr 0.15 at 10 years, +110k jobs

name: Ramp of the second-round revenue channel (other_revenue) after exposure begins
source: M2 with the eight-year phase-in of the simulated reform stripped out (inferred); low ≈ OFCE
note: Spending channels follow exposure at once (people retire on the day); pension contributions too; only the GDP-type revenue lags.

name: Cour des comptes: one year of AOD (63 vs 64) on the pension-system balance
source: Cour des comptes, 20 Feb 2025: 63 → +€5.8bn of spending in 2035; 65 → up to −€8.4bn
note: Asymmetric: a lower floor binds fewer people than a higher one. Deflated to each year at 2%.

name: DREES/COR cost of the 2026 suspension
source: COR June 2026, p.105 and Tableau 2.5 (DREES Trajectoire); government lettre rectificative €0.1bn 2026 / €1.4bn 2027
note: Used as a calibration: € per cohort-year = 1.8 / the suspension's own exposure computed here.

name: Published costings
value: RN (Oct 2026): 9 / 2031 / p60 / pension; OFCE (2024): 15.6 / 2030 / repeal / gg; CNAV (Nov 2024): 16 / 2032 / repeal / pension; Zemmour (2024): 21 / 2030 / repeal / gg; Montaigne (2024): 34.7 / 2030 / repeal60 / pension
source: RN €9bn cruising, €1.9bn 2027 → €9.5bn 2031 (Terra Nova reading of the counter-budget); OFCE 'minimal cost of repeal' €9.5bn 2027, €15.6bn 2030; CNAV via AN amendments €16bn 2032; M. Zemmour €20–22bn 2030; Institut Montaigne €34.7bn 'à l'horizon 2027' for repeal + 60 with 40 annuités for pre-20 starters
note: Each is converted to € per cohort-year on the exposure of the measure it costs (repeal = 2023 path → 62), then re-applied to P1/P2. Montaigne's 2027 is read as a steady-state figure and placed at 2030.

name: GDP level effect per cohort-year of lower age, after 10 years
source: Mésange: +260k jobs for two cohort-years at 10 years → 130k per cohort-year ≈ 0.43% of employment × 0.8 relative productivity; OFCE +110k (−0.15%); Rexecode +1.1% GDP for the 2023 reform in 2030 (−0.55%)

name: Ramp of the GDP effect
source: declared, from the M2 path

name: Elasticity of R01, R02, R03, R04, R06 to GDP
source: declared
note: Expenditure fixed in euros, so the ratios also move. Revenue shares of GDP from the 2024 strict file.

name: GDP path for the ratios
source: engine reference scenario (0.5% real, 2% deflator)

name: Scope
value: general government, S.13, all compulsory schemes
source: committee, 20 Oct 2026
note: COFOG GF10_2 carries CNAV, the régimes spéciaux, the fonction publique and Agirc-Arrco; Agirc-Arrco follows the legal age with a lag (its own board) — assumed to follow.
